key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning predicted welding quality metrics more accurately than the multitask neural network, while multitask learning still offered strong shared-task generalization.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between shared-model efficiency and task-specific accuracy when estimating UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness for process optimization and quality control.
method: Built a multitask neural network with shared hidden layers and task-specific outputs.
Compared it against stacking ensemble learning on the same welding dataset.
Evaluated both models using RMSE and R² across UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
evidence_signal: On the reported test results, stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² for all three targets, with especially strong performance for UTS and weld hardness.
watch_item: The performance trade-off suggests stacking may be more accurate for individual outputs, but MTL may be preferable when data are limited or tasks are strongly related; results may not transfer without validation on new welding conditions.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
